The probability that at least one stock will increase is given by:
P(at least one increases) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B)

Since we want the greatest value for the probability that neither stock will increase, we need to minimize the probability that at least one stock will increase. P(at least one increases) = 0.56 + 0.74 - 0.56
P(at least one increases) = 0.74

Now we can find the greatest value for the probability that neither stock will increase:
P(neither) = 1 - P(at least one increases)
P(neither) = 1 - 0.74
P(neither) = 0.26

Therefore, the greatest value for the probability that neither of these two events will occur is 0.26.
